You have to go through a transformation together to form lasting relationships. It can be as simple as doing something for the first time ever, or as dramatic as adopting a new way of life. Relationships made in transition when you're vulnerable and depend on others are by far the most lasting.

Putting yourself out there is more than just being available to date, it's also a time to be open to growth and new experiences.

It sounds like you know all this because you're willing to go to a firing range, but I thought I'd chime in for anyone else reading.

Personally, I like to expose people to new bands and foods to start relationships. Not only does that create a novel experience for then to grow in a non-challenging way, but it also permanently cements you as a part of them if they love what you show them.

From there I go for something physically exerting or exciting. It could be rock climbing, shadow boxing, or even rollercoasters and motorcycles. Like before, it's better if they've never done it before. They associate you with the excitement, and you're halfway to a lifelong relationship.

Next, they have to see you be an expert at something. Let them watch you perform and get approval from others. Play instruments, be funny, out drink an Irishman. Whatever you do well, let them see you do it in public, or as public as it can be.

Lastly, you reveal something about yourself no one else knows, and you trust them with it. If that information remains a secret, you've got yourself a lifelong relationship.

A good relationship involves both people doing these things back and forth to gain each others respect and admiration. I've also begun something new. I am building a spreadsheet to track my progress. Right now, there are two worksheets within it: Approaches, and Interactions. It's really helping, I imagine for the same reason tracking my workouts and caloric intake really helps.

I have gotten to the point where I am able to regard approaches in a slightly more detached way. I've been reading "Bang" by Roosh V, and he made a very important point that never really occurred to me before: If a girl reacts poorly to my approach, she's only judging my approach. It's so simple and logical, but profound. It helps a lot, and also sort of segues into the notion of tracking activity.

That said, I did an experiment tonight. So, I was getting eyes from one girl who was in a pair. They were apparently waiting for a couple of guys. I got the eyes again, and sat down next to them. "Hi. How are you girls doing?" A polite response and reciprocation, and then something quick that I couldn't hear. Probably something about the fiancee that I learned about a little later. Their body language became cloistered, so I just ignored them at that point. The guys showed up a few minutes later.

I migrated to a slightly better vantage point, where I had a view of pretty much everything, though I was slightly out of the way. Well, while I was sitting scoping things out, people watching, and cataloging the male behavior that I was seeing (this was around 1100), I caught the same girl giving me eyes. That was a huge confidence booster. I laughed out loud. I waited a minute or two until the guys were at the bar getting more drinks, and walked up to her, with my phone held out on the dialer screen. I guess I thought I was being discrete. In any event, that's when I got the "I have a fiancee, I'm sorry." So I shrugged and went back to my seat.

When I sat back down, I noticed this one random guy, who was with his buddy, looking at me with this face. So I gave him this face until he looked away. At that point, I just started cataloging the IOIs I was getting from around the bar. There were quite a few. And the best part: I wasn't surprised.

Now, TRP, you may be asking, where did all this confidence come from?

Well, earlier, before I had gone to that tavern, I stopped in a local sports bar that I hadn't been to before. Sat down with a couple of old timers, chatted with them a bit, got a feel for the place. I noticed a woman walk in, look around, and move toward the far corner of the bar. I excused myself from the table I was at, and made my way to the bar, pretty much right in the eye line of this mysterious woman. My age, maybe a bit older (so early to mid thirties) Got some definite IOIs. Made my way over and opened.

The interaction was great. Eye contact, really steady, meaningful eye contact the whole time. Got a personal question, about my work. Ran a routine that I made up on the spot, which has since gone in my little notebook. It's an astronaut routine, and she loved it. Saw her ring, didn't stop or even mention it. She told me she had a fiancee, kept going. Got her number (!) a bit later. Don't even have her name. I asked her what I should put in for the contact name. She gave a classy, mysterious nondescript moniker, like something out of a Bogart movie. So that's what it says.

I got the distinct impression that she was "working" the eye contact as much as I was, mainly because I'm not usually that good at it. My general takeaway from that interaction is that she was seeking validation, in the form of attracting some attention. "I'm getting married, but I want to know I've still got it." sort of thing. I will call her in a few days, but I fully expect to never see her again. In addition to being a huge confidence booster, this was also a teachable experience:

The Power of Gab (I maybe be investing in some improv classes at some point, and I think I'm going to attend a few open mic nights - purely as a spectator)

What persistent eye contact feels like when she's interested. While it's still a significant hurdle to build that interest, now I know what it feels like. Yes, it's been quite a while since I've experience that kind of connection with a woman.

Routines can be fun! They should be fun!

Not all women are going to make it as easy on me as Classy did. But, if I continue to internalize the vibe, more women will find themselves drawn to me, and it will get easier. And the cycle perpetuates itself ad infinitum from there.

I need to start carrying around blank business cards. That way, I can write my number on one and slip it to a girl who is attached while allowing her to maintain the pretense the she's not a whore (which this one totally was). She may throw it out. Or she might text. The only guaranteed miss is the shot you don't take.
Tonight went well. I am beginning to internalize some aspects of The Vibe.
